title: Positive and negative reinforcement

draft.title: Positive and negative reinforcement
card: Reinforcement is a consequence that makes a behaviour more likely to happen again. In this use, positive and negative do not mean good and bad. They mean adding and removing.
something pleasant is added after a behaviour. A child who tidies their room and is given praise is more likely to tidy it again.
something unpleasant is taken away after a behaviour. A person who takes a tablet and the headache goes away is more likely to take one next time.
Both kinds make the behaviour more likely. Punishment is different, because it makes a behaviour less likely.
draft.remember: Positive adds and negative removes, but both reinforcers make a behaviour more likely.

a.q: Jun studies for a test and his parents then give him a bonus on his pocket money. He studies harder for the next test. What is this?
a.why: Something pleasant was added after the behaviour, and the behaviour became more likely. That is positive reinforcement. It is not negative reinforcement, because nothing unpleasant was taken away.
a.clue: Was something added or removed, and did the behaviour increase?

b.q: Priya's alarm beeps loudly until she gets out of bed and turns it off. She now gets up faster each morning. Which statement is correct?
opts: Negative reinforcement, as the unpleasant beeping is removed
Positive reinforcement, as getting up is a good outcome
Punishment, as the beeping is an unpleasant stimulus
Negative reinforcement, as her behaviour becomes less likely
b.why: The beeping is unpleasant and it stops after she gets up, so it is removed. Her behaviour becomes more likely, so this is negative reinforcement. It is not punishment, because punishment makes a behaviour less likely.
b.clue: What stops after she gets up, and what happens to the behaviour?

b.best: Negative reinforcement, as the unpleasant beeping is removed
